title: The Stag at the Pool
text:
On a hot day a stag came to a spring to drink. As he bent his head, he saw his reflection in the still water and stopped to admire it. His antlers were magnificent, tall and wide and branching. He was proud of them.

Then his eyes fell on his legs, and he frowned. They were so thin and spindly, so plain compared with the splendid crown on his head. He wished they were more handsome.

While he stood there admiring and complaining, a lion crept up to the pool and crouched to spring. The stag saw it just in time and bolted. On the open plain his slender legs carried him easily ahead of the lion, and he kept a safe distance as long as the ground was clear.

But then he ran into a wood, and his great antlers caught in the low branches. He twisted and pulled, but he could not free himself. The lion came up and seized him. As he died, the stag cried out that he had despised the legs that would have saved him and taken pride in the antlers that had destroyed him.
lesson: Take a hard look at what you value in yourself or your organization. The plain, useful strengths are often the ones that save you, while the showy ones can trap you.
